title: Egypt lifts import curbs, backs bigger private sector role to meet IMF demands
claim: Reuters reported that Egypt lifted a key import restriction and that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi approved a list of 62 economic activities the state would leave to the private sector to meet IMF conditions.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a concrete policy move and a presidential approval tied to IMF conditions.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as the president approving the list and to his government implementing the import-policy reversal; IMF conditionality and the dollar shortage were major external constraints.
contrary_evidence: The move was reactive and tied to IMF demands rather than an autonomous reform agenda.
The article notes continuing foreign-currency shortages and earlier devaluations.

title: US$ 500 Million Project Will Help to Strengthen Egypt's Food and Nutrition Security
claim: The World Bank approved a US$500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support food-security reforms; it tied the project to Egypt's Bread Subsidy Program and about one month of wheat supply for roughly 70 million low-income Egyptians, including about 31 million people under the poverty line.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous World Bank press release with specific project terms, beneficiary counts, and policy rationale.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government as the borrower-side authority and policy sponsor, though the shock context was heavily external.
contrary_evidence: The project is a response to crisis pressure, not proof of structural welfare improvement by year-end.
The same text emphasizes pandemic and Ukraine-war shocks.

title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
claim: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand Egypt's Takaful and Karama program, saying it covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022, that women were 74 percent of card holders/direct beneficiaries, and that 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with direct coverage, targeting, and distribution details.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government as the policy sponsor, though co-designed with the World Bank and focused on implementation through the Ministry of Social Solidarity.
contrary_evidence: This shows mitigation and targeting, not a full answer to poverty or labor-market weakness.
It does not prove that vulnerable households were adequately protected from inflation.

title: Protecting and Fulfilling the Rights of Children In Egypt
claim: UNICEF said poverty had risen despite government programmes, nearly 30 percent of Egyptians lived in monetary poverty, children in poorer backgrounds faced a triple burden of malnutrition, and at least 1 million school-age children with disabilities were out of school along with many refugee and migrant children.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country report is a strong local synthesis, but it is retrospective and not a direct audit of Sisi's personal choices in 2022.
period_fit: retrospective on the 2022 period and the immediate surrounding years
ruler_attribution: Country-level welfare context and criticism of government performance; attribution to Sisi is indirect through national policy responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes progress in mothers' and children's health and government programmes to expand basic services.
It is a retrospective synthesis, not a year-end implementation audit.

title: Recovering from COVID-19 Learning Losses
claim: UNICEF said marginalized children, especially migrant and refugee children, were below expected learning levels in literacy and numeracy after COVID-19, and that UNICEF was working with Egypt's education ministry and partners to reach close to 30,000 children with a remediation programme and assessment tools.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNICEF country story with explicit Egypt-specific remedial action and target group descriptions.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national education system under the Sisi government, but the remedial action was jointly implemented with UNICEF and external donors.
contrary_evidence: The story emphasizes learning loss and unequal access rather than a completed recovery.
It is a program description, not a final outcome evaluation.

title: Egypt (EGY) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
claim: UNICEF's Egypt country dashboard reports 2022 primary-school attendance at 97 percent and primary completion at 91 percent, with lower-secondary attendance at 85 percent and upper-secondary attendance at 70 percent.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source; the values are directly visible on the page.
ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; not a direct ruler-action measure.
contrary_evidence: High attendance does not eliminate quality or completion gaps for poorer and marginalized children.
The page does not isolate Sisi's personal contribution.

title: Egypt (EGY) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
claim: UNICEF's Egypt country dashboard reports 2022 safely managed drinking-water access at 79 percent and safely managed sanitation access at 57 percent.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source; the values are directly visible on the page.
ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; not a direct ruler-action measure.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard is outcome data, so it cannot isolate Sisi's personal contribution.
Significant gaps remain, especially in sanitation.

title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Egypt
claim: UNICEF's child-SDG dashboard for Egypt reports 3 percent of children in extreme poverty in 2022, 33 percent of children below the national poverty line in 2017, and 14 percent child-population coverage by social protection floors/systems in 2020.
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source with direct visible values and methodology context.
ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; useful mainly for identifying residual deprivation and limited coverage, not direct personal action.
contrary_evidence: The page mixes different reference years and cannot by itself measure 2022 ruler performance.
It does not separate national policy effects from inherited trends.

title: WHO Egypt and Ministry of Health and Population celebrate physicians on Family Doctor Day
claim: WHO and Egypt's Ministry of Health held a 2022 conference for 200 primary health-care workers and said family physicians are the first point of contact for essential care and health emergencies, while WHO continued technical and capacity-building support for family medicine.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report on a concrete 2022 event and support activity.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Ministry of Health under the Sisi government, though the source also reflects WHO and USAID support.
contrary_evidence: A conference and training support do not prove system-wide service quality.
The source emphasizes staffing shortages and the need for further investment.

title: WHO Egypt works towards improving the hospital sector in Egypt
claim: WHO said it worked with Egyptian health authorities in August 2022 to develop the national strategic plan for the hospital sector, and that Egypt was taking active steps to implement universal health insurance and build a more resilient health system.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report describing a specific policy workshop and the government's UHI implementation direction.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-era health ministry and linked institutions, though implementation was collaborative with WHO and higher-education bodies.
contrary_evidence: The source is a workshop report, not an outcome evaluation.
It notes system-development challenges rather than completed reform.

title: Health systems strengthening towards universal health coverage
claim: WHO said it actively supported Egypt's Ministry of Health in pursuing universal health coverage and described Egypt's health system as fragmented, with unequal access and large out-of-pocket burdens, while arguing that an equity-driven health sector can help break the illness-poverty cycle.
source_confidence_reason: WHO country programme page is a strong institutional source, but it is general background rather than a 2022 event report.
ruler_attribution: Country-system context rather than a discrete Sisi action, though it addresses the system his government governed.
contrary_evidence: The page is framed as long-run support and baseline context, not a year-specific performance audit.
It does not measure 2022 delivery.

title: Improving Wastewater Services Program - Upper Egypt
claim: Egypt signed a CHF 7.2 million grant on 10 February 2022 for an Aswan water project under SDG 6, with related goals of good health and reduced inequalities.
source_confidence_reason: Official ministry project page with a dated financing agreement and explicit location/objective information.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government through its international-cooperation ministry, though the project was donor-financed and locally implemented.
contrary_evidence: The page gives project metadata rather than completion or impact results.
It is a grant announcement, not an implementation audit.

title: Sustainable Rural Sanitation Services Program for Egypt
claim: The World Bank said its rural sanitation program for Egypt aimed to increase access to and services of rural sanitation in Beheira, Dakahliya, and Sharkiya, improving citizens' well-being and protecting agricultural soil.
source_confidence_reason: Dated World Bank project infographic with explicit geography and objective.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the broader Sisi-era state program and its development partners, not to a single ministerial decision.
contrary_evidence: The infographic is a goal statement, not proof of finished service expansion in 2022.
It does not quantify completed households or outcomes.

title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
claim: The Egyptian military spearheaded the state-led investment strategy pursued under Sisi and controlled a vast economic portfolio spanning infrastructure, housing, industrial zones, media, and land/import approvals.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed analytic paper with explicit sourcing and concrete institutional description.
period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing the Sisi model operating through 2022.
ruler_attribution: Direct to Sisi's presidency and the military apparatus he empowered; it shows policy and network control, but not personal enrichment by itself.
contrary_evidence: The same paper notes military-managed infrastructure and low-income housing can deliver some public goods.

title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
claim: Military financial details were kept behind a firewall; the military's costs were described as opaque and based on privileged access to land, contracts, tax and customs exemptions, and conscript labor, while senior retirees in civilian posts reproduced favoritism and patronage.
source_confidence_reason: Analytic paper ties opacity and patronage to named institutional mechanisms and cites IMF and prior research.
period_fit: Published in 2022 and directly relevant to the 2022 economic structure.
ruler_attribution: Direct to the presidentially backed military economic model; this supports network privilege and concealment, though not a documented personal-family windfall.
contrary_evidence: The military and government claimed cheaper public goods and development value for some projects.

title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
claim: President Sisi and the security apparatus dominate policymaking, the Administrative Control Authority is under Sisi's control and lacks credibility, transparency, and impartiality, and the government provides very little transparency about spending and operations.
source_confidence_reason: Major country report with direct institutional findings and consistent with other monitoring sources.
ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Sisi because the report explicitly places the ACA and policymaking under his control; it does not prove his private enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The report still acknowledges formal anticorruption mechanisms and state institutions, even though it says they are weak and ineffective.

title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
claim: The National Human Rights Strategy was drafted without consultation with independent human rights organizations or public engagement, and Amnesty says authorities used it as propaganda to conceal growing repression ahead of COP27 while blaming security threats, economic challenges, and citizens for the rights crisis.
source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporary rights reporting based on on-the-ground monitoring and a named report.
period_fit: Directly about a 2022 strategy and repression surrounding COP27.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to the authorities under Sisi's rule and to a strategy launched under his auspices; it does not prove his personal knowledge of every false or misleading element.
contrary_evidence: Authorities did launch a formal strategy and presented it publicly as a rights commitment.

title: World Report 2023: Egypt
claim: Sisi declared 2022 the year of civil society, but civil society members still faced arbitrary travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal investigations in retaliation for activism, and thousands remained unjustly detained for peaceful activism.
source_confidence_reason: Annual rights report summarizing 2022 events with a stable country chapter and consistent sourcing.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the government Sisi led; it shows retaliation and continued coercive control rather than personal financial gain.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes some detainees were released in piecemeal fashion, but says repression continued.

title: Factbox-National political dialogue in Egypt follows years of crackdowns
claim: Reuters reports that Sisi said Egypt holds no political prisoners and that human rights are promoted by jobs and housing, while rights groups estimated tens of thousands detained; the same factbox notes the 2013 protest law banned protests without prior police approval.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch with direct quotation and contemporaneous contrast to human-rights reporting.
period_fit: Published in 2022 and discussing the 2022 dialogue and Sisi's public line.
ruler_attribution: Direct because the no-political-prisoners claim is Sisi's own statement; the protest-law context is state action under his rule.
contrary_evidence: Egyptian officials said the crackdown targeted terrorists and saboteurs, not political opponents.

title: Militarizing the Supreme Constitutional Court
claim: For the first time, an Armed Forces officer was appointed to Egypt's highest court; military judiciary head Salah al-Ruwainy was sworn in as Supreme Constitutional Court first deputy justice.
source_confidence_reason: Independent Egyptian outlet reporting a clearly identified presidential appointment with date and institutional detail.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because it followed a presidential appointment; it indicates politicization of a neutral institution, though not personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show personal financial self-dealing, only institutional militarization.

title: President El-Sisi Appoints Major General Amr Adel as Chairman of Administrative Control Authority
publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
claim: Sisi appointed Major General Amr Adel Ali Hosni as acting head of the Administrative Control Authority, the state's leading anti-corruption body.
source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential notice of the appointment with exact date and office.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment; it suggests control over anti-graft oversight but does not prove a specific corrupt act by Sisi himself.
contrary_evidence: The source does not show what Amr Adel did after appointment or whether the body later acted independently.

title: New head of Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court sworn in before Sisi
claim: Sisi issued a decree appointing Boulos Fahmy Eskandar, a long-serving judge, as head of the Supreme Constitutional Court from the pool of longest-serving deputy chairs.
source_confidence_reason: Mainstream Egyptian outlet reporting a formal judicial appointment with institutional detail and career history.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment under a formal selection rule; this is a counterexample of a professional, non-kin appointment, but one case does not establish a broad pattern.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes the president has appointment authority, so the process still reflects executive influence.

title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
claim: The IMF said Egypt's program would strengthen governance, accountability, and transparency, reduce the state footprint, adopt a more robust competition framework, and expand targeted social transfers and spending on social assistance, health, and education.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release describing the authorities' policy package and conditional reforms.
period_fit: Directly about 2022 reform negotiations and the 2022 policy package.
ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is an IMF-supported program negotiated with the authorities, so it shows policy direction and external pressure more than personal integrity by itself.
contrary_evidence: The need for IMF support and the reform conditions themselves indicate that stronger transparency and governance were not yet established practice.

title: President Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
claim: Sisi approved a state ownership policy document that set a three-year plan to expand private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent, withdraw from 62 business activities, and announce the state's reasoning at each step.
source_confidence_reason: Mainstream report on an official policy document with concrete sectoral targets and implementation rules.
period_fit: Directly about a 2022 presidential policy decision.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential approval, but implementation was still gradual and subject to strategic-security exceptions, so the document is commitment evidence rather than proof of practice.
contrary_evidence: The same article says the policy would be implemented gradually and that strategic/security considerations could limit withdrawal.

title: Egypt Economic Conference 2022
publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
claim: Sisi opened Egypt Economic Conference 2022 and framed the country’s situation as requiring clear and decisive measures to address a decade-long economic and social crisis
source_confidence_reason: Official presidential page is authoritative for what Sisi launched and said, but the language is broad and rhetorical rather than proof of execution.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about the ruler's stated program.
ruler_attribution: Strong for program articulation because the page records Sisi's own event and framing; weaker for implementation because the statement is programmatic rather than operational.
contrary_evidence: Rhetorical framing alone does not show actual delivery or durable reform.

title: Egypt's Economic Update - April 2022
claim: Egypt allowed the exchange rate to depreciate and raised policy rates, while the government introduced a LE130 billion mitigation package that expanded cash transfers and other relief measures
source_confidence_reason: World Bank is a strong independent macro source, and the page gives specific policy actions and dates.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the ruler-period macro response.
ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the measures were taken by the CBE and government under Sisi's political authority, but external shocks and some central-bank autonomy limit personal attribution.
contrary_evidence: Global price shocks and Ukraine-war spillovers were major drivers of the crisis, so outcome attribution is incomplete.

title: US$ 500 Million Project Will Help to Strengthen Egypt's Food and Nutrition Security
claim: The World Bank approved a $500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support reforms to strengthen food security and nutrition
source_confidence_reason: The project announcement is explicit, dated, and operational, with a clear target population and financing amount.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and responsive to an external shock during the ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project supports a government bread-subsidy and food-security response, but the financing and implementation are shared with the World Bank.
contrary_evidence: The project addresses an external shock and donor-financed support, so it does not by itself prove domestic administrative competence.

title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
claim: The World Bank announced $500 million to expand Takaful and Karama, which covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022 and sent most cash to Upper Egypt, while the government expanded social safety nets to absorb price shocks
source_confidence_reason: The page provides concrete coverage, distribution, and funding details for a named social-protection program.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to late-year crisis response and policy follow-through.
ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the government is an implementing partner and the program expansion is an identifiable state action, though the World Bank remains a co-financier and some design predates 2022.
contrary_evidence: The press release is partly World Bank framing and does not independently verify full on-the-ground delivery by year-end.

title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
claim: Egypt faced a spike in inflation and large portfolio outflows; foreign exchange buffers fell sharply since March 2022; the CBE allowed the exchange rate to depreciate and raised rates; the government announced social mitigation packages; growth was expected to slow and poverty could rise
source_confidence_reason: This is a detailed World Bank country monitor with specific macro indicators and policy responses, but it still reflects a forecast environment under external shocks.
period_fit: Directly late-2022 and contemporaneous with the target period.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: the macro deterioration is partly external, but the policy response is attributable to the authorities under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: The report emphasizes that the Russia-Ukraine war, supply-chain disruptions, and tightening global conditions were major drivers, limiting clean ruler attribution.
